detail.title: State-Substitute Governance in Armed Conflict:The Formation, Maintenance and Boundaries of Accountability of the Detention System in North-Eastern Syria
detail.abstract: In the study of armed conflict, detention is typically defined as an ancillary arrangement to security control, military custody or counter-terrorism management; however, when formal state capacity continues to fail in conflict zones, detention itself may evolve into a governance mechanism with institutional continuity. This paper focuses on the detention system in northeastern Syria, using the facilities in al-Shaddadi and the regional detention network in which they are embedded as a case study, to address the current research gap regarding the detention practices of non-state armed actors, which are 'visible yet insufficiently theorised'. Drawing on multilingual open-source materials, institutional tracing, node identification, the reconstruction of chains of responsibility, and normative analysis, this paper proposes the analytical concept of 'detention-based alternative state governance' to identify how detention networks have transformed from temporary wartime arrangements into enduring de facto governance structures. The study finds that the detention system in northeastern Syria has transcended the scope of single-point security management, exhibiting an organisational form characterised by the interlocking of facility networks, armed control, subject classification, transfer and diversion, external support, and information interfaces. In this context, the sustained takeover and institutionalised operation of detention functions by non-state actors have driven the formation of alternative governance structures, whilst the embedding of external support has enhanced the system's sustainability whilst simultaneously exacerbating the blurring of accountability boundaries. Furthermore, whilst the system demonstrates strong functional continuity in governance, it remains in a state of prolonged instability regarding procedural foundations, clarity of accountability and normative legitimacy, thereby exhibiting a structural tension characterised by 'high control-low legitimacy'. The theoretical significance of this paper lies in advancing detention from a peripheral security component in existing research on alternative governance to a core institutional entry point for understanding the formation, maintenance and attribution of responsibility in state alternative governance; its practical value lies in providing a more structural analytical framework for the monitoring, accountability identification and evidence chain construction within conflict detention systems, whilst offering a testable foundation for the further development of related research at both academic and practical levels.

title: Non-Truthful Mechanism Design for Revenue Management in Queueing Systems
affiliations: Catholic University of Portugal (UCP) - Catolica Lisbon School of Business and Economics and University College London - UCL School of Management

detail.title: Non-Truthful Mechanism Design for Revenue Management in Queueing Systems
detail.abstract: Service providers commonly cater to heterogeneous customers with private types. It is well known that in such situations, rather than offering a single class of service, providers can extract additional revenue by offering two service classes-a regular class and a premium priority class-featuring differentiated prices and lead times. Traditional menu design in such settings has focused on incentive-compatible (IC) mechanisms, which induce rational customers to truthfully reveal their private types through their choice of service class. These mechanisms are built on the premise that customers will misrepresent their types whenever doing so is advantageous. In practice, however, customers often face procedural or behavioral constraints that make such misrepresentation difficult or undesirable. We show that the presence of such unconditionally honest customers-even in arbitrarily small proportions-can make non-truthful (NT) mechanisms, under which some misrepresentation occurs in equilibrium, strictly optimal. These NT mechanisms can yield higher revenue than any IC mechanism and, in contrast to IC designs, never rely on delay tactics (i.e., artificially inflating lead times) to screen types. We characterize the structure of optimal NT mechanisms, identify the conditions under which they outperform IC alternatives, and show that NT mechanisms, when optimal, also improve social welfare. Finally, we discuss managerial insights and practical considerations for the implementation of such NT mechanisms in real service settings.

title: The Protective Effect of Role Clarity on NHS Employee Wellbeing: A Moderation Analysis

detail.abstract: Using the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model, this study examined the moderating effect of role clarity on the relationship between work demands and psychological distress among NHS employees and whether this protective effect varies with occupational groups. The results confirmed that work demands significantly predicted distress, whilst role clarity demonstrated both direct protective effects and a significant moderating effect. However, subgroup analyses revealed occupation specific patterns with no significant moderation emerging amongst non clinical staff. This result highlights the importance of occupation specific approaches to staff wellbeing.

title: Predictive Maintenance for Additive Manufacturing Through Integrated Lean Six Sigma and Artificial Intelligence Approaches

detail.title: Predictive Maintenance for Additive Manufacturing Through Integrated Lean Six Sigma and Artificial Intelligence Approaches

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Authors declare no conflict of interests.

detail.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) systems require high precision and consistent thermal-mechanical control, yet they remain vulnerable to machine degradation, print instability, and defect formation that often lead to costly downtime. Traditional maintenance strategies, i.e., reactive and preventive approaches, do not suffice for the AM environment, as they cannot comply with real-time machine conditions or address the complexities and failure mechanisms associated with advanced AM technologies. This study examines the current body of literature to comprehensively evaluate Predictive Maintenance (PdM) as a transformative approach for AM, integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI), multisensor monitoring, and Lean Six Sigma (LSS) methodologies to anticipate failures before they occur. It expands upon the fundamentals of Condition-Based and Statistical-Based PdM in AM, reviews AI techniques including machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and hybrid models, and describes data acquisition pipelines involving thermal, acoustic, optical, vibration, and machine log signals. It also evaluates case studies in industrial AM settings to highlight current implementations of AI-enabled PdM, revealing both the opportunities and the constraints imposed by data scarcity, sensor limitations, and model generalization challenges. Further discussions include emerging topics such as federated learning for distributed AM networks and the evolving role of digital twins within Industry 5.0 frameworks. Collectively, this review assesses how PdM, AI, and LSS can function in tandem to reduce downtime, enhance process stability, and accelerate the transition toward autonomous and self-correcting AM systems.

title: Mitigating the Bullwhip Effect in Demand Forecasting
affiliations: KU Leuven - Faculty of Economics and Business, KU Leuven - Faculty of Economics and Business, KU Leuven and KU Leuven - Faculty of Business and Economics (FEB)

detail.title: Mitigating the Bullwhip Effect in Demand Forecasting

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by Research Foundation Flanders (FWO) under grant numbers 1107926N and 12AZX24N.

detail.abstract: Mitigating the bullwhip effect is a key strategy to increase supply chain efficiency, and forecasting models play a crucial role in amplifying or mitigating this effect. Existing methods for bullwhip mitigation provide only limited control over the trade-off between forecast accuracy and bullwhip effect mitigation through model evaluation and selection, or rely on reactive corrections such as order smoothing. We propose a novel loss function approach to proactively train machine learning forecasting models to mitigate the bullwhip effect. By combining forecast errors and bullwhip effect into a single loss function and jointly minimizing their weighted sum during model training, our method provides fine-grained control over the trade-off between these two competing metrics. Extensive validation on the M5 dataset shows that our method effectively mitigates the bullwhip effect when the weight given to the bullwhip term is sufficiently large, and that substantial mitigation can be achieved with only a limited loss in forecast accuracy.

title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism From the Mechanistic Paradigm to the Living Systems
affiliations: Jiangsu Normal University Kewen College

detail.title: The Metabolic Theory of the Economic Organism From the Mechanistic Paradigm to the Living Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. The author has no financial, institutional, or personal relationships that could have influenced the research presented in this work. All theoretical development and writing were conducted independently.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research does not involve human participants, personal data, or animal subjects. Therefore, ethical approval was not required. The study is a theoretical work in economics and social science.

detail.abstract:
This book proposes the Economic Organism-Metabolism Theory (EOMT), a systematic reframing of economic analysis grounded in thermodynamics rather than classical mechanics. The central argument is that mainstream economics has long operated under a mechanical equilibrium metaphor borrowed from Newtonian physics. EOMT replaces this with the Second Law of Thermodynamics: the economy is an open dissipative system that continuously generates metabolic waste, resists entropy through ongoing productive activity, and is subject to irreversible time. This shift is structural, not metaphorical — it changes what the discipline can see.

The core analytical engine is the dynamic value equation: dV/dt = A − C − S, where A is anabolic metabolism (value creation), C is catabolic metabolism (depreciation of ordered structures), and S is entropy loss (efficiency dissipation from institutional friction). Value is redefined as negentropy — accumulated ordered structure. Economic growth is the sustained excess of A over C and S, not the maximization of a scalar output.

The book's five parts develop this framework systematically. Part I establishes the physical and anatomical foundations, including the thermodynamic redefinition of value and the functional anatomy of the economic organism (firms as cells, finance as circulatory system, government as nervous and immune system). Part II constructs the metabolic physiology: the waste theory (material, value, and information waste), the Metabolic Excretion Law (crises are forced excretion of accumulated waste, not system failures), and a reinterpretation of money as blood and interest rates as hormones — with monetary velocity, not quantity, as the primary diagnostic variable. Part III examines dynamic processes: a multidimensional metabolic efficiency index, a unified anatomy of three canonical crises (the Great Depression, Japan's Lost Decades, and the 2008 crisis), and theories of government pathology identifying four failure modes including immune capture and neural oscillation disorder. Part IV extends the framework to culture (a four-stage culture-metabolism co-evolution model), political institutions (democratic vs. authoritarian governance as metabolic regulatory architectures matched to development stages), and demography (demographic decline as slow-variable indicator of deep metabolic structural failure, explained by a four-layer mechanism including the Intergenerational Metabolic Mismatch Hypothesis). Part V scales to the global system: a trophic level framework for international inequality, a two-dimensional analysis of great powers versus small states (metabolic integrity × trophic level), case studies of Europe's metabolic aging and Africa's developmental arrest, and a unified theory of involution-hegemony-lock-in showing that structural inequality operates through the same metabolic physics simultaneously at global, national, industrial, and labor-market scales.

EOMT's primary contributions are: (1) a unified thermodynamic foundation replacing the mechanical equilibrium metaphor; (2) the C/S distinction — separating stock-level depreciation from flow-level efficiency loss — enabling policy precision that conventional aggregate indicators cannot provide; (3) the integration of HANPP and entropy debt as hard physical constraints on the core metabolic equation, grounding economic analysis within planetary boundaries; (4) the Metabolic Excretion Law providing a pre-crisis diagnostic framework rather than post-hoc model-fitting; (5) metabolic lock-in as a policy target analytically prior to conventional antitrust, shifting intervention from market concentration outcomes to metabolic capital ownership structures; and (6) a cross-scale unified framework demonstrating that the multiplicative layering of contemporary inequality follows from the same metabolic physical laws at every scale. The theory explicitly acknowledges three limitations: the social Darwinism misreading risk, the determinism risk (addressed via the iPS cell analogy — lock-in is an activation energy barrier, not historical fate), and the incomplete theorization of collective agency as a constitutive metabolic variable.

title: Return Concerned Adaptive Control of Product Offerings
affiliations: University of Waterloo, McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management and University of Colorado at Boulder

detail.title: Return Concerned Adaptive Control of Product Offerings
detail.abstract: Product returns are a major operational challenge in online retail, where lenient return policies and post-purchase uncertainty generate both substantial costs and delayed information. We study a dynamic assortment optimization problem in which a retailer must learn customer purchase and return behavior over time while return outcomes are observed with delay and only within a finite return window. The problem is motivated by a collaboration with a major European fast-fashion retailer.  We develop a unified two-stage purchase-return model in which the purchase decision and the subsequent keep/return decision are generated from shared latent primitives. To solve the resulting learning problem, we propose COBRA (Confidence Bounds for Return-Aware Assortments), an epoch-based algorithm that combines productlevel likelihood estimation, learning of the in-window return-delay profile, and optimistic assortment selection under joint uncertainty. We establish a regret bound that makes explicit the effects of delayed and window-censored returns, and we complement it with a lower bound showing that partial return observability fundamentally affects the learning problem. Numerical experiments on both synthetic instances and real retail data show that incorporating return information can substantially improve profit performance relative to return-blind approaches.  Our results show that returns should be treated not only as a cost, but also as a delayed information source for merchandising decisions. In the tested settings, return-aware learning improves assortment quality and often yields lower realized return volumes as a secondary operational benefit. The analysis also highlights a managerial tradeoff in return-window design: expanding the window makes more return information observable, but it also increases the temporal difficulty of learning from recent purchases.

title: Machine Learning-Aided Material Selection, Parameter Optimization, and Process Monitoring in Laser-Based Metal Additive Manufacturing
affiliations: University of Toronto - Department of Materials Science and Engineering

detail.title: Machine Learning-Aided Material Selection, Parameter Optimization, and Process Monitoring in Laser-Based Metal Additive Manufacturing
detail.abstract: Laser-based metal additive manufacturing (AM) technologies, such as laser powder bed fusion and laserbased directed energy deposition, have been broadly adopted in a wide range of industries, including the aerospace, automotive, biomedical, and energy sectors. These technologies require cross-scale coordination spanning six orders of magnitude, involving complex interactions between laser parameters, feedstock properties, and thermal-fluid dynamics. The resulting high-dimensional datasets span materials, processing parameters, laser-metal interaction, and final part properties, posing significant challenges to understanding intricate processing-structure-property (P-S-P) relationships. Recent advances in machine learning (ML), with its capacity to uncover hidden patterns and correlations from large, high-dimensional datasets, present a transformative approach to accelerate discovery and optimization in metal AM. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances and challenges in employing various ML methods across key stages of the metal AM workflow. We explore the application of ML in the following aspects: (1) The ML-aided selection of materials, covering new materials development and metal powder selection; (2) The ML-aided optimization of processing parameters, including the establishment of processing maps and the implementation of optimization strategies; (3) The ML-aided in situ monitoring and quality assurance of the AM processes using sensors, including acoustic emission, visible light, infrared, synchrotron X-ray, and multi-sensor systems. Moreover, we examine the characteristics, limitations, and data requirements of various ML models in each of these domains, guiding model selection and experimental design. By adopting an ML-centric perspective, this review aims to inform future research directions, support the development of more autonomous metal AM systems, and accelerate the optimization of laser-based metal AM.

detail.abstract: For the avoidance of doubt: 1) This catalogue presents and analyzes a variety of options for reducing the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet. detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) research increasingly relies on large, interdisciplinary teams to address complex societal challenges. detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether CEOs with legal expertise (hereafter, 'lawyer CEOs') influence acquirer shareholder wealth in mergers and acquisitions (M&As). Using U.S. firms from 1991 to 2023, we find that acquiring firms with lawyer CEOs exhibit a significantly higher acquisition propensity and deal completion rates. Acquirers led by lawyer CEOs also experience higher cumulative abnormal returns, particularly under high information asymmetry, weak governance, and adverse legal environments. Notably, CEOs with legal expertise mitigate valuation uncertainty and information asymmetry in stock-financed deals, reducing the negative effects of stock payment on acquirer announcement returns and deal synergies, particularly for larger acquirers, firms with low book-to-market ratios, and those with limited access to legal advisors.

detail.title: Orbital Authority: Governance Architecture for Autonomous Space Operations

detail.abstract:
Space operations present unique governance challenges for autonomous systems: communication latency, deterministic orbital mechanics, and compressed decision timelines prevent continuous human oversight. No existing framework addresses the authority computation problem for autonomous space systems operating beyond real-time human control.

This paper introduces Orbital Authority, a domain-specific governance architecture for autonomous space operations, extending the AUTHREX framework into the orbital domain. The architecture integrates sensor trust evaluation, deception detection, authority computation, and enforced deliberation windows adapted to Keplerian constraints and communication delays ranging from seconds to hours.

A five-tier Keplerian decision taxonomy (K1–K5) is developed to map operational scenarios to appropriate governance modalities, ranging from routine conjunction avoidance to time-critical counterspace engagements. The framework incorporates dynamic sensor confidence modeling, escalation risk quantification, and multi-agent consensus protocols to ensure safe and accountable autonomous decision-making.

Analytical evaluation across representative space operation scenarios demonstrates how governance intensity can be scaled to match temporal and strategic constraints. The proposed architecture provides a computable foundation for trusted autonomy in contested orbital environments, with implications for space security, defense policy, and the long-term sustainability of the orbital commons.

As organisations navigate increasingly dynamic environments, traditional hierarchical structures are often insufficient to meet the demands of simultaneous excellence across multiple dimensions. The matrix organisational design, characterised by dual or multiple reporting lines, offers a flexible and adaptive solution, enabling organisations to balance competing demands and enhance collaboration, knowledge sharing, and innovation. Drawing on empirical evidence and cross-sectional studies, this report offers actionable recommendations for the successful implementation and optimisation of matrix organisational design, with a focus on public organisations and other complex contexts, including from the EU.

title: Do Projects Learn across Space and Time? Evidence from the Olympics
affiliations: University of Oxford - Said Business School, University of Oxford - Said Business School, IT University of Copenhagen and University of Oxford - Saïd Business School

detail.title: Do Projects Learn across Space and Time? Evidence from the Olympics
detail.abstract: Do projects learn across space and time? The Olympics, themselves among the largest publicly funded programmes in the world, offer a unique empirical setting. Theoretically, the Games seem ideal for generating 'positive learning curves', driving down costs from one iteration to the next. In practice, they do not. Drawing on the concept of 'myopia of learning', we argue that spatiotemporality (geographic distance, temporal gaps, and the temporary organizational form of each host committee) combines to block higher-level learning. Our analysis of cost overruns from 1960 to 2024 reveals no sustained improvement over 64 years. Tactical learning abounds, but none aggregates into strategic improvement. We propose four strategies for overcoming the spatiotemporal barrier (incremental, centralizing, decentralizing, and real options), arguing that radical reform is required.

title: Early Intervention Practice with Child Welfare-Involved Children and Families: Strategies for Engaging Referred Families
affiliations: University of New Hampshire

detail.title: Early Intervention Practice with Child Welfare-Involved Children and Families: Strategies for Engaging Referred Families
detail.abstract: Infants and toddlers involved in the child welfare system are at elevated risk for developmental delay, yet many eligible children do not receive Part C Early Intervention (EI) services despite federal referral mandates. This qualitative constructivist study examined how EI professionals engage families referred following substantiated maltreatment. Twenty-one EI professionals from hospital-based, community-based nonprofit, and state-run programs participated in in-depth ethnographic interviews. Grounded theory analysis with constant comparison and member checking identified engagement as a consistent challenge to enrollment and service delivery. Participants described systemic barriers including inaccurate referral information, inconsistent interagency communication, conflation of EI with child protective services, perceived coercion, and complex parental mental health and substance use needs. Professionals reported adaptive strategies emphasizing relationship building, transparent communication, flexible first contacts, and strengthened collaboration with child welfare partners. Engagement practices prioritized family-centered support and responsiveness to immediate social needs alongside developmental concerns. Findings suggest that improving EI access for child welfare-involved families requires structural reforms including standardized referral processes, cross-agency training, and expanded workforce preparation in trauma-informed and behavioral health practice. Strengthening collaborative infrastructures may enhance engagement, enrollment, and continuity of EI services for vulnerable young children.

detail.abstract: ABSTRACT  Job satisfaction is a crucial determinant of nurses’ well-being, productivity, and overall performance, directly influencing the quality of healthcare delivery. Nurses play a vital role in patient care, and their level of satisfaction significantly impacts patient outcomes, organizational efficiency, and staff retention. This study aims to identify the key factors influencing job satisfaction among nurses and to examine the challenges they encounter in their professional roles. The research focuses on critical determinants such as workload, work environment, interpersonal relationships with colleagues and supervisors, compensation, and opportunities for professional growth. These factors collectively shape the overall job satisfaction of nurses and influence their motivation, commitment, and performance within healthcare institutions.In addition, the study explores common problems faced by nurses, including long working hours, emotional and physical stress, inadequate staffing, and limited resources. Such challenges often lead to burnout, reduced efficiency, and increased turnover, thereby affecting the quality of patient care. Furthermore, the study highlights significant occupational risks faced by nurses, including physical hazards, biological and chemical exposure, psychosocial and mental stress, workplace violence, and structural risks such as extended shifts and insufficient support systems.Understanding these factors and challenges is essential for developing effective strategies to enhance job satisfaction and create a supportive work environment. detail.abstract: Background: Physician burnout rates remain elevated despite substantial organizational investment in wellness and coaching programs. Peer-reviewed evidence confirms these interventions reduce individual distress symptoms; the same evidence confirms they do not move the indicators that predict whether physicians stay-engagement, job satisfaction, depersonalization, and meaning at work. This persistent gap between intervention investment and retention outcomes suggests the field is treating the symptom of a mechanism it has not yet named. Proposed Mechanism: The author proposes a four-stage developmental and behavioral mechanism-Selection, Indoctrination, Activation, and Systemic Lock-that accounts for the origin, persistence, and resistance to symptom-level intervention of physician disengagement. The mechanism locates the source of disengagement not in the clinical environment, but in childhood, where survival patterns are formed; in medical school admissions, which select for candidates who already carry those patterns; in residency training, which hardens them over a decade; and in the institutional systems of attending life, which continue reinforcing the same logic indefinitely. Framework: The Nine Core Wounds™ is a proprietary clinical taxonomy of nine survival patterns that the proposed mechanism produces - each identifiable, predictable, and associated with a distinct behavioral signature visible to department leadership. Implications: If the proposed mechanism is correct, effective intervention must operate at the level of the operating strategy itself - not at the level of the distress symptoms it produces. The Source Code Protocol™ is proposed as a behavioral framework designed to meet that criterion. The author calls for controlled research comparing operatingstrategy-level interventions to symptom-level interventions on engagement, retention, patient satisfaction, and malpractice risk outcomes.

detail.abstract:
Uninsurable By Design extends the KEV governance series from litigation and capital-markets analysis into insurance, reinsurance, prudential capital and market stability. Its central claim is not that artificial intelligence introduces a difficult new class of operational risk. It is that, where V = 0 governs consequential reliance, a growing category of AI-assisted exposure no longer fits cleanly within the ordinary conditions of insurable risk. Insurance retreat therefore does not merely reveal the problem. It intensifies it.

The paper argues, first, that verification absence alters the kind of risk the market is being asked to absorb by destabilising definable peril, assessable probability, bounded loss, attributable cause and fortuity. Second, it identifies a recursive mechanism, the insurance retreat spiral, through which narrowed cover, exclusions and retained exposure worsen the insured pool and accelerate further retreat. Third, it shows that this dynamic extends beyond insurance through substrate-level correlation, prudential capital, supervisory convergence and market confidence into a wider macroeconomic transmission mechanism.

The paper further argues that the correlation problem is deeper than vendor concentration alone. Even where the commercial landscape appears more diverse, transformer-based, token-generative systems operating under V = 0 may still share the same verification-absent flaw. A discovered failure should therefore not always be treated as an isolated event, but may be the first legible fragment of a much larger latent failure population distributed across firms, sectors and jurisdictions.

The paper also includes threshold instruments for underwriting committees, renewal decision rules and falsifiable boundary tests against the strongest anticipated objections. Drawing on insurance practice, financial supervision, market evidence and historical precedent, it concludes that the market is not pricing AI risk in the ordinary sense. It is discovering that a category of AI-assisted exposure does not yet qualify as insurable risk. Once transfer begins to weaken, the consequence is no longer confined to individual firms. It propagates through pricing, capacity, supervision and balance-sheet fragility.

title: Essay: Fluent, Certain And Wrong By Design
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Essay: Fluent, Certain And Wrong By Design
detail.abstract:
Generative AI is often discussed as though it were a reasoning system awaiting further refinement. This essay argues that the more accurate description is architectural: a system optimised to produce fluent, persuasive and contextually appropriate outputs without any intrinsic, consequence-bearing capacity to verify whether those outputs are true at the point of generation. Within the KEV framework, Knowledge may be vast and Experience may deepen behaviourally, but Verification remains absent. This condition, expressed as V = 0, has major governance consequences once institutions begin to rely on generated outputs in consequential decisions.

The essay introduces the Synthetic-Plausibility Effect to describe the way increased fluency, contextual fit and confidence can be misread as justified reasoning, even where intrinsic verification is absent. It also introduces the ACU classification (Artificially Confabulating and Untrustworthy) as a more accurate label than “hallucination” for failure modes that arise from normal generative operation rather than malfunction. Drawing on governance, liability and institutional decision-making logic, the essay argues that organisations are building reliance before they have established defensibility, thereby accumulating epistemic debt that may crystallise under audit, litigation, regulatory inquiry or investor scrutiny.

This essay serves as the diagnostic entry point to the wider KEV governance framework, published through a linked series of papers, companion papers and technical notes on Zenodo and SSRN.

title: Organizational Meaning Science: The Meaning Loop as a System-Level Model of Meaning Dynamics

detail.title: Organizational Meaning Science: The Meaning Loop as a System-Level Model of Meaning Dynamics
detail.abstract: Meaning is widely acknowledged in leadership and organizational research, yet it is typically treated as an internal psychological experience or as a byproduct of communication processes. These approaches struggle to explain persistent interpretive divergence, escalation, and instability within organizations, even when leadership behaviors and communication practices appear effective. This article introduces Organizational Meaning Science as a conceptual framework that positions meaning as a relational and dynamic property of human systems rather than a purely individual cognitive state. Central to this framework is the Meaning Loop, a recursive model describing how signals, interpretation, behavior, and feedback interact to stabilize or destabilize meaning over time. By conceptualizing meaning as a system-level phenomenon, the article reframes leadership influence as a form of interpretive stewardship and provides a foundation for examining how meaning alignment, divergence, and drift emerge within organizational systems. The article situates Organizational Meaning Science within existing leadership and organizational theory and establishes a basis for future research on the dynamics of interpretive alignment and stability in organizations.

title: Organizational Meaning Science: Integrating Process and Structure in Meaning Dynamics

detail.title: Organizational Meaning Science: Integrating Process and Structure in Meaning Dynamics
detail.abstract: Organizations do not operate only through coordination and control; they operate through meaning. Leaders signal direction, teams interpret priorities, and individuals translate those interpretations into action. Although prior research has examined sensemaking, communication, and organizational climate, these perspectives remain fragmented in explaining how meaning forms, stabilizes, and shifts across organizational levels. Building on prior work in Organizational Meaning Science, which introduced the Meaning Loop as a process model of interpretive dynamics, this paper extends the framework by conceptualizing meaning architecture as the structural system through which meaning is formed, transmitted, and sustained. Meaning is reconceptualized as a system-level property shaped by layers, nodes, and pathways that influence how signals are interpreted and how meaning circulates. The framework develops key constructs-including meaning alignment, neutrality, and drift-and explains how these states emerge through ongoing feedback between communication, interpretation, and behavior. By linking micro-level interpretive processes with macro-level patterns, the paper advances a multi-level account of how meaning stabilizes, diverges, and evolves over time. This work contributes to organizational theory by integrating structure and process within a unified model of meaning formation and identifying mechanisms that shape meaning dynamics across organizational systems.

detail.abstract: We estimate the causal impact of River Basic Health Units (Unidades Básicas de Saúde Fluviais, UBSF) - mobile vessels that deliver primary care along fixed river routes in the Brazilian Amazon - on a broad set of health outcomes. Exploiting the staggered municipal rollout between 2009 and 2023, we combine the Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) difference-indifferences estimator with 1:5 pre-treatment nearest-neighbor matching. We find robust positive effects on hospital deliveries of 1.5-2.5 percentage points across estimators, operating primarily through a direct referral channel rather than through increased prenatal consultations. We find no statistically significant effects on overall infant or neonatal mortality, consistent with insufficient statistical power given the small birth denominators in treated municipalities. Beyond maternal outcomes, we document that UBSF reduces malaria mortality by approximately 58% (IRR = 0.42, p = 0.011) and leprosy hospitalizations by 64% (IRR = 0.36, p < 0.001), while increasing recorded Chagas disease cases-consistent with improved detection of a prevalent but historically undiagnosed endemic infection. Taken together, the results indicate that mobile primary care in extreme-geography settings serves simultaneously as a gateway to the formal health system, a referral mechanism for safe delivery, and a treatment platform for endemic tropical diseases.

detail.abstract: Background: Digital data streams, including social media and mobility tracking, offer new opportunities for real-time public health surveillance during rapidly evolving crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic. Public emotional responses, captured through social media platforms, may influence compliance with public health interventions, yet their interaction with policy measures remains insufficiently understood. Objective: This study examines the relationship between population-level stress measured by negative emotions, public health policy implementation, and mobility behavior during the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, with a focus on how emotional responses interact with stay-at-home orders to shape behavioral outcomes. Methods: We conducted a county-level longitudinal ecological analysis using publicly available data from February to April 2020. Public stress levels were measured using geolocated Twitter data on negative emotions toward COVID-19, while mobility behavior was assessed using SafeGraph social distancing metrics as a proxy for staying at home. Public health policy exposure was operationalized as the number of days stay-at-home orders were in effect. Random-effects regression models were used to evaluate associations between emotional signals, policy duration, and mobility, including interaction effects. Models controlled for demographic, socioeconomic, epidemiological, and political factors. Results: Higher levels of stress, characterized by negative emotions, were significantly linked to greater reductions in mobility (β=18.83, p<0.001). The duration of stay-athome orders also positively correlated with decreased mobility and notably moderated the relationship between stress levels and mobility (β=0.82, p<0.001), suggesting that emotional responses intensified the impact of policy measures. Other interventions, such as school and business closures, demonstrated less consistent associations with mobility. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the value of integrating social media-derived emotional signals with mobility data for public health surveillance. Emotional responses appear to play a critical role in shaping behavioral compliance, particularly when reinforced by clear policy interventions. These findings suggest that incorporating real-time emotional monitoring into public health strategy may improve the effectiveness of policy communication and implementation during future health emergencies.

detail.abstract: This study investigates whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) preparedness acts as a catalyst for structural upgrading or as a barrier to entry for African economies within Global Value Chains (GVCs). Combining, for the first time, the granular GVC positioning indicators (upstreamness) from Mancini et al. (2023) with the IMF's AI Preparedness Index (AIPI), we construct a novel dataset covering 11 African countries from 2000 to 2022. We address cross-sectional dependencea critical issue in a sample of interconnected economies-by employing Common Correlated Effects (CCE) and Interactive Fixed Effects (IFE) estimators. Our results reveal a nuanced reality. While standard models suggest a positive association between AI and upstreamness, our preferred IFE specification shows that, in isolation, AI preparedness is associated with a significant decrease in upstreamness (β =-0.042, p < 0.001), suggesting a risk of "premature automation" that confines countries to downstream segments. However, this effect is conditional on absorptive capacity: the interaction between AI and human capital reverses this trend, indicating that AI acts as a complement to, not a substitute for skills. Furthermore, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) positively contributes to GVC upgrading only once common shocks are controlled for, highlighting the importance of knowledge transfer over mere capital inflows. Our findings imply that without strategic investments in "AI-ready" human capital and coordinated continental policies (e.g., within the AfCFTA), AI risks exacerbating technological bifurcation rather than fostering leapfrogging.

detail.abstract:
Introduction: Medical tourism decision-making is characterised by high uncertainty, perceived risk, and severe information asymmetry, particularly in domestic contexts where patients select healthcare providers without prior experiential knowledge. Despite the growing importance of international healthcare accreditation, systematic evidence on how accreditation signals are prioritised relative to service quality attributes and psychological factors remains limited. 

Methods: This study integrates Signaling Theory and the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-OR) framework to develop a hierarchical model of patient revisit intention toward JCI-accredited hospitals in domestic medical tourism. A Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) was employed to elicit and quantify expert judgments under uncertainty. Data were collected from a panel of 15 purposively selected experts-representing academia, JCI-accredited hospitals, medical tourism enterprises, and public health agencies-through a two-round Delphi process and structured pairwise comparison questionnaires. 

Results: JCI accreditation signals account for 61.73% of total global weight, substantially outweighing service quality (21.41%) and psychological states (16.86%). Patient safety standards rank first among all sub-criteria (global weight = 0.3029), followed by brand reputation (0.1572) and quality certification (0.1572). Within service quality, assurance and reliability are prioritised over tangibility and affective dimensions. Trust in the hospital is the most salient psychological factor. 

Discussion: These expert-based findings suggest that accreditation signals account for the largest share of expert-elicited priority weight in domestic medical tourism, consistent with the proposition that they may function as a primary credibility threshold preceding service quality evaluations in high-uncertainty healthcare contexts. Hospitals in emerging markets, such as Vietnam, may therefore consider JCI accreditation a high-priority strategic signal for strengthening revisit potential rather than merely a supplementary credential.

title: The Ideology of the Priority of Creation Over Destruction (IPSN)

detail.title: The Ideology of the Priority of Creation Over Destruction (IPSN)
detail.abstract:
After watching the 2012 Bad Movie on YouTube , I realized that human culture is currently structured with the wrong priorities. The YouTube movie easily showed scenes of murder and fighting, but censored the sex scenes. This inspired me to write this article.

Humanity has very strange priorities when it comes to censoring film footage: you can't show sex, but you can show murder and dismemberment . What's wrong with our priorities? Maybe this is the problem with birth rates? Why is there a cultural taboo against showing genitals, but not against showing murder? Maybe because we are told to censor by laws based on morality that has failed? Why do we suppress our sexual instinct in memes , but not our desire to kill? Why do states allow themselves to wage wars where millions of people die, but forbid orgies for even 1,000 people? Who is worse or who is better: a prostitute or a soldier?

title: Teaching Students to Think Critically About AI-Generated Business Analysis: What I Learned from Testing ChatGPT and Gemini

detail.title: Teaching Students to Think Critically About AI-Generated Business Analysis: What I Learned from Testing ChatGPT and Gemini
detail.abstract: This study systematically tests how AI tools handle business frameworks across three core MBA disciplines (Marketing Strategy, Consumer Behaviour, Strategic Management) to understand implications for business education. Through five controlled experiments, I discovered a Framework Hierarchy: AI achieves 0% framework naming in business strategy disciplines but 60% in behavioural disciplines, revealing that framework performance depends on framework type, not business discipline. Psychology-based frameworks with descriptive names (Reference Price, Involvement Theory) achieve higher AI naming rates, while business taxonomies (Ansoff Matrix, Resource-Based View, Porter's strategies) are invisible in AI output. This creates discipline-specific teaching challenges and exposes the "Prompt Engineering Paradox"-students need existing framework knowledge to effectively prompt AI. The study bridges corporate L&D measurement principles (activity vs learning vs capability metrics) with academic assessment, offering practical frameworks for teaching in the AI era.

detail.abstract: This paper examines Azerbaijan's post-2020 economic strategy as a form of reconstructioncentered geoeconomic statecraft. Through analysis of infrastructure policy, investment frameworks, and regional connectivity initiatives between 2020 and 2024, the study demonstrates how postwar recovery has been systematically transformed into an instrument of regional economic repositioning. The research introduces the concept of reconstruction-driven geoeconomics to describe Azerbaijan's integration of physical rebuilding, transit diplomacy, and energy diversification into a unified development narrative. The strategy performs multiple functions: consolidating domestic economic control over liberated territories, enhancing bargaining leverage in regional connectivity negotiations, and reframing post-conflict recovery as a regional public good. Economic analysis focuses on large-scale infrastructure deployment, foreign direct investment signaling, and transport corridor planning, alongside structural tensions between rapid capital mobilization and political risk. Findings indicate that while Azerbaijan's reconstruction model effectively accelerates short-term growth momentum and regional engagement, its long-term sustainability remains contingent upon political normalization, institutional capacity, and inclusive economic integration.

detail.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence into organizational decision-making has produced a critical and largely unaddressed structural problem. Leaders are consulting AI before they have independently defined the problem, gathered evidence, or audited their own cognitive biases. Research on automation bias documents the consequence: humans anchor to AI recommendations and fail to correct for AI errors even when those errors are detectable, introducing new categories of decision failure rather than reducing existing ones (Lyell & Coiera, 2017; Kücking et al., 2024). The human-AI collaboration literature has identified this risk extensively. It has not produced a named, sequenced framework that governs when AI enters the leadership decision process. This paper introduces LOGIC-the first structured decision framework designed specifically to position AI input at a governed step within a sequenced human reasoning process. The five-step sequence-Locate the problem, Observe the facts, Guard against bias, Investigate with AI, Choose and check-is built on a single architectural principle: human epistemic foundation must precede AI consultation. Steps 1 through 3 require the decision-maker to independently define the problem, establish an evidential baseline, and conduct a bias audit before AI is introduced in Step 4. This sequencing is not incidental. It is the structural mechanism by which the framework prevents automation bias from corrupting the decision. No existing leadership decision framework integrates AI as a bounded, sequenced step with an explicit rationale for its position in the process. Cynefin (Snowden & Boone, 2007) classifies decision environments. The OODA Loop (Osinga, 2007) optimizes decision speed. Neither governs the human-AI interface. LOGIC fills that gap, grounded in dual-process theory (Kahneman, 2011), metacognitive reflection research (Becker et al., 2023), and the empirical automation bias literature (Kücking et al., 2024; Horowitz & Kahn, 2024). Its central claim: the sequence in which humans reason and AI contributes determines whether AI improves or degrades leadership decision quality.

title: Beyond Static MCDM: Mitigating "Incentive Blindness" in Automated Software Vendor Selection via a Dual-Agent Supervision Architecture (DASA)

detail.title: Beyond Static MCDM: Mitigating "Incentive Blindness" in Automated Software Vendor Selection via a Dual-Agent Supervision Architecture (DASA)
detail.abstract: The selection of software vendors in global supply chains has traditionally relied on static Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) methods such as AHP or TOPSIS. While effective for ranking known attributes, these methods fail to detect dynamic risks, particularly deceptive compliance claims regarding data sovereignty and security (e.g., SOC2, GDPR). This study proposes a novel paradigm: Generative Multi-Agent Negotiation (GMAN). We introduce a framework where Large Language Model (LLM)-driven agents simulate adversarial negotiations to interrogate vendors and uncover non-compliance. Through a comparative simulation (N = 50), we identify a critical vulnerability in monolithic autonomous agents which we term "Incentive Blindness," where agents prioritize cost minimization over safety constraints (100% failure rate in single-agent architectures). To address this, we propose a Dual-Agent Supervision Architecture (DASA), which decouples the "Procurement Negotiator" from a distinct "Compliance Validator." This multi-role framework increased the risk detection rate from 0% to 100%, effectively mitigating hallucinated compliance without sacrificing economic objectives. These findings suggest that structural agent orchestration, rather than prompt engineering alone, is requisite for safe, automated enterprise procurement.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether women exhibit differences in productivity when working in office-based environments compared to remote work settings. Using a cross-sectional correlational design, survey data from female employees in New South Wales, Australia were analyzed to assess self-reported productivity across work environments. title:

Work, Meaning, and the Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence.

detail.title:
The Wretched and the Machine: 
Work, Meaning, and the Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence.
detail.abstract: Why do people work? This question, deceptively simple on its surface, conceals one of the deepest tensions in modern political economy. This essay argues that the social construction of work as intrinsically meaningful has historically served those who benefit from labor more than those who provide it — and that artificial intelligence now forces a confrontation with this contradiction that can no longer be deferred. Drawing on the political economy of Daron Acemoğlu and Simon Johnson, the philosophy of Seneca and the Stoics, the critical pedagogy of Paulo Freire, and the poetry of Bertolt Brecht, this essay examines how technological progress has consistently promised universal prosperity while concentrating its benefits among those with the power to shape its direction. Particular attention is given to the differential impact of AI on developing economies — especially those with fragile legal and institutional frameworks — and to the question of whose values, whose feedback, and whose vision is embedded in the intelligent systems now reshaping the world of work.

detail.abstract: As artificial intelligence increasingly assumes persuasive roles in healthcare, education, and social services, understanding how AI persuaders compare to human persuaders becomes essential for designing compassionate AI systems. This study investigates whether and how human and AI persuaders differ in perceived credibility, attractiveness, and persuasion effectiveness, while examining the mediating and moderating mechanisms that shape these outcomes. Drawing on source credibility theory and human-machine communication frameworks, we conducted a 2 (Persuader: AI vs. Human) × 2 (Context: Consequential vs. Inconsequential) between-subjects experiment with 508 Chinese participants, complemented by semi-structured interviews with 22 participants. Results revealed that human persuaders were perceived as significantly more credible (d =-0. 2 5) , more attractive (d =-0. 2 4) , and more effective (d =-0. 2 3) than AI persuaders delivering identical messages. Both credibility and attractiveness fully mediated the persuader type-effectiveness relationship, with credibility accounting for 62% of the total indirect effect. Prior attitudes toward AI moderated credibility and effectiveness perceptions, with positive attitudes eliminating the human advantage, while decision context consequentiality showed no moderating effects. Qualitative findings revealed six novel AI characteristics-immediacy, psychological safety, cognitive extension, low-inputhigh-output interaction, dialogue flexibility, and emotional risk minimization-that constitute alternative sources of persuasive appeal beyond traditional interpersonal frameworks. We develop a hybrid credibility model and technology-enabled attractiveness paradigm that extend classical persuasion theory to AI contexts. These findings carry significant implications for compassionate AI design: because credibility inherently encompasses benevolence and concern for audience welfare, designers should prioritize credibility-building mechanisms over anthropomorphic simulation, and leverage technology-enabled compassion-psychological safety, non-judgmental interaction, emotional risk minimization-as authentic pathways to compassionate outcomes.

title: Fair Ranking Design for Medical Crowdfunding

detail.title: Fair Ranking Design for Medical Crowdfunding
detail.abstract: Medical crowdfunding platforms promise to help those unable to afford healthcare, yet campaigns by less socially connected individuals systematically raise fewer donations. We study whether this inequality reflects unconnected donors' limited awareness-rather than their preferences-and whether platform ranking design can mitigate it. Using data from Qingsongchou, China's largest medical crowdfunding platform, which implements a policy to randomly assign promotion timing and ranking, we show that a front-page promotion leads to a 257% increase in donations, and that the effect is concentrated among donors unconnected to the campaigner. We estimate a structural model of donation choice under limited consideration and find that 64% of donors consider at most the top four ranked campaigns. Counterfactual simulations show that equality-oriented rankings, which prioritize campaigns with fewer social connections, meaningfully reduce inequality in donation outcomes with only small costs to platform revenue. However, a donor-surplus-maximizing ranking would significantly increase both revenue and inequality, creating a tradeoff in platform ranking design.

detail.abstract: This paper studies the relationship between child allowances and demographic regimes in an overlapping generations economy with family transfers, pay-as-you-go pensions, and child quality investment. In a stationary benchmark with inelastic labor supply, discrete fertility generates decline, replacement, and growth demographic regimes. The benchmark yields two closed-form thresholds, one, two, or three self-confirming steady states under a common permanent allowance, permanent policy cutoffs that eliminate decline or sustain growth, and a welfare cutoff for education pressure. detail.abstract: This study presents the development and validation of a revised and integrated scale for measuring pro-environmental behavior, addressing limitations in existing instruments such as the Pro-Environmental Behavior Scale (PEBS). The scale proposed in this study, the Pro-Environmental Behavior and Attitudes Scale (PEBAS), expands the behavioral domains to include recycling habits, sustainable consumption of textiles and electronics, exposure to environmental content on social media and social networks, and beliefs about the causes of climate change and the efficacy of mitigation efforts. The 20-item survey was administered to a sample of 640 university students in Italy. Psychometric validation followed a two-step procedure: exploratory factor analysis identified a five-factor structure, and confirmatory factor analysis confirmed the model's fit. Additionally, measurement invariance confirmed that the model allows for valid comparisons of latent constructs across genders. Compared to the previous scale, the PEBAS offers a more comprehensive and contextually relevant measure of pro-environmental behavior, particularly suited to younger populations. The findings support the scale's utility for academic research, the public sector, and policy evaluation, contributing to the broader goal of evidence-based environmental policymaking and behavioral interventions.

detail.abstract: Synthetic control (SC) methods are widely used to estimate the effects of policy interventions, especially those targeting specific geographic regions, referred to as units. These methods construct a weighted combination of untreated units, forming a "synthetic" control that approximates the counterfactual outcomes of the treated unit had the intervention not occurred. Although neighboring areas are often selected as controls due to their similarity in observed and unobserved characteristics, their proximity can lead to spillover effects, where the intervention indirectly impacts control units, potentially biasing causal estimates. To address this challenge, we introduce a Bayesian SC framework with utility-based shrinkage priors. Our approach extends traditional penalization techniques (i.e., horseshoe, spike-and-slab) by incorporating a utility function that combines covariate similarity and spatial distance. This provides a metric that guides the data-driven selection of control units based on their relevance and spillover risk, which is assumed to increase with spatial proximity. Rather than outright excluding neighboring units, the method balances bias and variance by reducing the importance of potentially contaminated controls by spillovers. We evaluate the proposed method through simulation studies at varying spillover levels and apply it to assess the impact of Philadelphia's 2017 beverage tax on the sales of sugar-sweetened and artificially sweetened beverages in mass merchandise stores.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Social and Social Policy, Vol. 6, No. 2, pp. 63-75, 2007

detail.abstract: An area of study that is relatively neglected by comparative welfare state experts is the comparison of health care systems. Since the early 1990s, health care systems in Europe have experienced a myriad of changes, just like pensions systems, their counterpart. The systems of health care provision applied in Europe are varied a great deal. The Swedish system follows for the most part the ideal-typical model as set by Esping-Andersen, yet the overall change of paradigms in the international arena has also altered the Swedish health care system. This study focuses in detail on the comparative advantages of the Swedish health care system, while also focusing on the new shortcomings on the operational level. Sweden, it is concluded, has survived the turbulent times of the past two decades. The negative experience of quasi-marketbased solutions did not put an end to public dominance in health care provision in Sweden. In long-term, international comparison, Sweden constitutes one out of a number of strong examples of the success in public health care delivery.

detail.title: Fiscal Forecast Errors in East Africa

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper explores the nature and underlying factors contributing to fiscalslippages in selected East African countries from 2000 to 2024. Slippages are proxied by the budget forecast errors as captured in WEO projections by IMF Staff. Our findings indicate that budget forecasts tend to be systematically optimistic with actual budget balances typically falling short of projected balances, primarily due to spending overruns and, to a lesser extent, revenue shortfalls. Unexpected revenue shortfalls largely arise from indirect taxes (VAT and customs), whereas spending slippages are predominantly influenced by public investment, goods and services and social protection expenditures. The optimism bias is more pronounced in situations where the budget is in deficit, during economic booms, among commodity-exporting countries, in the absence of an IMF program or fiscal rules, and when fiscal institutions are weak. These results are robust to excluding potential outliers, expanding the sample to other SSA countries, and controlling for country specific effects as well as potential endogeneity bias.

detail.title: The Rise of Cyber Events and Digital Fraud in the Financial Sector

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Cybersecurity and digital fraud are closely intertwined in financial services, as vulnerabilities in digital systems enable both institutional cyber incidents and fraud against users. This paper uses publicly available data to review and examine important trends underlying the growing concern of digital fraud. The results indicate that, across 20 industry sectors in 162 countries, cyber events in the financial sector accounted for about 10 percent over the past decade and were concentrated primarily in the banking and securities sectors. Cyber-enabled fraud has nearly tripled but remains underestimated due to underreporting and data gaps across jurisdictions. Credit transfers and credit cards dominate scam payments, with rising reports of payment fraud in some jurisdictions alongside increased crypto‑related cyber events and fraud. Industry studies also suggest that scam losses represent a higher share of gross domestic product in developing economies, while advanced economies tend to incur higher individual losses. Targeted regulatory and infrastructure measures have been taken to strengthen trust in digital finance in some jurisdictions.

detail.title: Institutions for Industrial Policy

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We propose an institutional architecture for the successful implementation of industrial policy inspired by the Asian Miracles—Japan, Korea, Taiwan Province of China, Singapore, and Hong Kong SAR. The key institutional arrangement is a leading agency, accumulating sector-specific knowledge through continuous experimentation and feedback from markets, to design the sector- and context-appropriate package of policies, which is a priori unknown, and coordinate its implementation. We also postulate a 4A model of institutional features of the leading agency: Ambition-Agency, Autonomy, Accountability, and Adaptability. We draw strong parallels with the rise of independent central banks, inferring concrete steps to achieve these characteristics.

detail.title: AI and Coder Employment: Compiling the Evidence

publicationDetails.journalName: Board of Governors: Finance & Economics Discussion Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: We evaluate whether LLMs have had any discernible impact on the aggregate labor market so far.  We focus on occupations that are computer programming-intensive, motivated by data showing that coding is one of the most LLM-exposed tasks.  Linking O*NET to CPS we find that aggregate employment of coders has decelerated sharply since the introduction of ChatGPT.  Using a novel control variable for industry-level shocks we show that the deceleration is not attributable to the exposure of coders to slowing industries, suggesting instead that coders experienced an occupation-specific shock around the introduction of ChatGPT.  Coder employment has continued to grow in recent years, though much more slowly than it did pre-2022.  We validate the industry-level control variable by examining historical examples of occupations that experienced either occupation-specific or industry-level shocks.  We also provide statistics on the agreement rates between different measures of AI exposure.

title: Explaining Latin America’s Decreasing Skilled Wage Premium
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF)

detail.title: Explaining Latin America’s Decreasing Skilled Wage Premium

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Skilled wage premia in Latin American countries have continued declining, albeit more slowly and unevenly. Is the decline driven by demand or supply? This paper proposes a novel adaptation to the demand-supply decomposition framework by incorporating directed technical change (DTC), specifically  supply-induced skill-biased technical change that acts to increase the wage premium. DTC counters the traditional substitution effect through which higher education wage attainment reduces the skill premium. Therefore, DTC makes adjusted inferred demand changes less skill biased than the standard framework’s traditional inferred demand changes. We apply the framework to ten Latin American countries over three periods, namely the length of the sample, the period between maximum wage premia and 2015, and since 2015. In our baseline results, DTC is quantitatively significant while the substitution effects remain important. Traditional demand shifts were skill biased over the length of the sample including since 2015 but our novel adjusted demand shifts were skill neutral. During the period between maximum premia and 2015, unadjusted demand shifts were skill-neutral and adjusted demand shifts favored unskilled workers. Equivalently, sizeable DTC effects imply wages would have fallen significantly faster in the absence of DTC. For an alternative elasticity of 1.25, DTC effects are smaller, supply effects are bigger, and adjustments to demand effects are smaller. For alternative supply measures, the results are relatively robust.
